title: Constructibility of a locally closed lisse coefficient extension
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, and let $\Lambda=E$ for a finite intermediate extension $\mathbf Q_\ell\subset E\subset \overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, or $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with the recorded condensed coefficient sheaves. For every locally closed immersion $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ and lisse $\Lambda_S$-module $L$ [sk-lem-coefficient-heart], let $a_!L$ be the canonical extension [det-lem-coefficient-heart-filtration], defined by open extension into the scheme-theoretic image followed by closed direct image. Its degree-zero derived object $(a_!L)[0]$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] is bounded constructible in the finite constant scalar model convention [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

proof.text: Factor a into the open immersion into its scheme-theoretic closure followed by the closed immersion into X. Every open in either ambient space is quasi-compact by Noetherianity, so the complementary open immersions satisfy the quasi-compactness hypotheses.

Use the condensed open-closed recollement comparisons and the existing disjoint-support pullback vanishing lemma. The open unit identifies the open restriction of u_!L with L; the complementary restriction is zero. Closed recollement similarly identifies the closed restriction of i_*M with M and its open restriction with zero. Finite locally free modules have finite constant models: the inverse image of the finite free module on the point is finite free of the same rank, since the monoidal pullback preserves finite biproducts.

Combine stratifications first for an arbitrary predicate on schemes with maps to X, using the existing open-closed concatenation. Then specialize this predicate to finite constant local models of the module restriction, transporting models by the pullback-composition isomorphism. Apply the open case and then the closed case to the two factors of the canonical extension. For the degree-zero derived object, boundedness is immediate; its zeroth cohomology is the module, up to the single-functor comparison, and all other cohomology vanishes. Constructibility transports under isomorphism and a zero module has a rank-zero constant model.

theorem coefficientHeart_lisse_extension_constructible (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (Λ : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) RingCat.{u + 1})
    [IsCommMonObj (coefficientHeartRingObj Λ)]
    (_hΛ : (∃ E : IntermediateField ℚ_[ℓ] (PadicAlgCl ℓ),
      FiniteDimensional ℚ_[ℓ] E ∧ Λ = Profinite.padicSubfieldCondensedRing ℓ E) ∨
      Λ = Profinite.padicAlgClCondensedRing ℓ)
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (a : S ⟶ X) (ha : IsImmersion a)
    (L : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology S) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (coefficientHeartRingObj Λ) S))
    (hL : IsLisseCoefficientModule (coefficientHeartRingObj Λ) L) :
    constantModelBoundedConstructible (coefficientHeartRingObj Λ) X
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
        ((coefficientHeartLocallyClosedExtension (coefficientHeartRingObj Λ) a ha).obj L))
